## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_with_retry` allows up to 10 attempts and defaults to 10, which breaks the 5-attempt cap in the project policy, so this must be fixed before merge. The same pull request loosens that policy, but the base rule is the one this change has to meet.

## Changes
This pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`, with a default and maximum of 10 attempts, along with tests and a one-line text fixture. It also edits the retry rule in `AGENTS.md` to raise the cap from 5 to 10.

## Critical
- app/net.py:19 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5 — When an upstream is down, a call with the default `attempts=10` (line 13) makes 10 fetches, and `1 <= attempts <= 10` accepts values up to 10. This breaks AGENTS.md:5: "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5. Unbounded retries have caused outages when an upstream was down." Your edit to that line in this pull request raises the cap with an unverified claim that "the upstream now sheds load itself." — During an upstream outage, each caller sends twice the retry load the policy allows, which is the outage pattern the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Set the default and bound to 5, and update the docstring, the `ValueError` message, `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count`, and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range` to match; change the policy in a separate, reviewed change if that is the intent.
